## Overview

The European Physical Society (EPS) has awarded its 2026 Europhysics Prize to physicists Jairo Sinova, Libor Šmejkal, and Tomas Jungwirth for discovering altermagnetism, a third fundamental class of magnetism that had gone unrecognized for over a century, according to the [European Physical Society](https://www.eps.org/2026-eps-europhysics-prize-for-outstanding-achievement-in-condensed-matter-physics-announced/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (713 words, within the 400-1200 range) following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Clear, professional, and free of hedging or filler. The Analysis section correctly contextualizes altermagnetism against the historical ferromagnet/antiferromagnet dichotomy without overstating the finding's novelty beyond what the prize citation claims.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three source snapshots were read in full from disk (gunzip + HTML-to-text extraction) and cross-checked sentence-by-sentence against every claim, quote, and specific number in the article. sha256 of each decompressed snapshot was independently recomputed and matched the manifest exactly, confirming snapshot integrity. (1) sources/2026-07/european-physical-society-awards-2026-europhysics-prize-for-discovery-of-altermagnetism/source-0.html.gz (press.uni-mainz.de, JGU press release, 200 OK, sha256 7b1a8814... verified) — confirms the three laureates, the EPS Condensed Matter Division prize, Sinova's SPICE directorship, the verbatim Sinova quote ('This award recognizes a fundamental discovery that challenged one of the most established paradigms in condensed matter physics. Discovering that an entirely new magnetic phase had remained hidden for more than one hundred years demonstrates that even the most mature scientific fields can still hold fundamental surprises.' — word-for-word match), Šmejkal's 2016-2024 Mainz tenure and his three current affiliations (Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences — all verbatim matches), the 2022 symmetry classification, and ARPES/electrical-transport experimental confirmation. (2) source-1.html.gz (eps.org official prize announcement, 200 OK, sha256 e69c522e... verified) — confirms the exact laureate list and spelling 'Tomas Jungwirth' (no 'h'; note JGU's own page inconsistently uses 'Thomas' once, but the article correctly follows the EPS's authoritative spelling and attributes it to EPS), the verbatim quote 'a third distinct elementary magnetic phase, one that combines seemingly incompatible properties of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets whilst exhibiting entirely different quantum phenomena' (exact match), the phrase 'considered for a century as mutually exclusive' used in the Analysis section (exact match), 'more than 200 candidate materials' (exact), direct observation in 'materials including MnTe and CrSb' (exact), 'more than a thousand subsequent studies' spanning magnetism/superconductivity/quantum materials/materials science (exact), the September 22, 2026 CMD32 Graz presentation date and the '42nd edition since 1975' figure (exact), Sinova's Texas A&M affiliation and Jungwirth's Czech Academy of Sciences / University of Nottingham / Tohoku University affiliations (all exact, from the photo-caption block), and the ultrafast/energy-efficient computer-memory and AI-hardware application language (exact). No monetary prize value is mentioned in either official source, consistent with the article's 'What We Don't Know' item. (3) source-2.html.gz (phys.org, archive_fallback: true — live URL returned 200 but the script used the Wayback Machine capture per its fallback policy; this is the canonical snapshot per the skill's guidance to treat archive_fallback content as authoritative) — this is a Science-X-network syndication of the same JGU press release ('Provided by Universitaet Mainz'), independently republished on a third domain with its own editorial fact-check badge; it corroborates the three laureates, the prize, and the September 2026 CMD32/Graz presentation, exactly as the article claims. No source required a live WebFetch fallback — all three snapshots saved successfully and were read from disk only. No hallucinated quotes, no misattributed facts, and no orphan source URLs were found: every URL cited in article.sources appears in the body and vice versa.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim, number, date, quote, and affiliation in the article was traced to and confirmed by the cited snapshot content. No fabrications, no paraphrase-inside-quote-marks issues, no conflation of separate claims. The one internal inconsistency found was in the JGU source itself (a stray 'Thomas' vs. 'Tomas' spelling), not in the article, which correctly uses the EPS's authoritative spelling and attribution.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Superlatives ('third fundamental class of magnetism', 'a century') are all directly attributed to the sources rather than asserted independently.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ (including all of 2026-07) for 'altermagnet', 'europhysics', 'sinova', 'smejkal', and 'jungwirth' — no prior or overlapping coverage found. concerns: The automated script's only finding is that eps.org and press.uni-mainz.de are not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt. Both are official, directly authoritative sources (the prize-granting society itself, and the press office of the university employing one of the three laureates) squarely within the editorial policy's preferred category of 'official sources' and 'academic institutions.' This is judged to be a source-allowlist maintenance gap, not a source-quality or factual defect, so it does not warrant a corrections record — there is no incorrect fact for a reader-facing correction to describe.
recommendations: Add eps.org and press.uni-mainz.de to config/source_allowlist.txt so future submissions citing these legitimate, frequently-relevant physics sources don't need a manual override each time.
